_comment: Which simplified 3D cell each cell type is drawn as (pipeline/_cell-families.mjs; step 13 builds the models, step 11 points each cell type at one). A cell type takes the family of the first rule whose Cell Ontology class is the cell type itself or one of its CL ancestors (step 06), so specific rules come before general ones. Cell types no rule matches get the generic cell. Epithelial families add microvilli or cilia when a rule under 'apical' matches. A cell type gets no nucleus when its family has none or a rule under 'noNucleus' matches; step 12 fails the build if such a cell type's model draws a nucleus. Shape and apical rules use CL classes that imply shape in standard histology where CL has no shape class of its own (CL's 'columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell' does not say which).

red-blood-cell.label: Red blood cell
red-blood-cell.noNucleus: Mature human red blood cells have no nucleus (Cell Ontology: 'In mammals, mature erythrocytes are biconcave disks containing hemoglobin').

platelet.label: Platelet
platelet.noNucleus: Platelets have no nucleus (Cell Ontology: 'A non-nucleated disk-shaped cell formed by extrusion from megakaryocytes').

rules.label: pancreatic endocrine cell
rules.note: Islet cells are neither nerve cells nor lining cells, so no simplified shape fits them.

rules.label: enteroendocrine cell
rules.note: Hormone-making cells within the gut lining.

rules.label: neuroendocrine cell
rules.note: Cell Ontology files neuroendocrine cells under neuron, but they have no axon or dendrites.

rules.label: cell of skeletal muscle
rules.note: HRA's ASCT+B tables use this term for the fibers of named skeletal muscles.

rules.label: beige adipocyte
rules.note: Its many small lipid droplets do not fit the fat cell shape, which has one large droplet.

rules.label: brown fat cell
rules.note: Its many small lipid droplets do not fit the fat cell shape, which has one large droplet.

rules.label: microglial cell
rules.note: Resting microglia reach out with long, branching processes.

rules.label: Langerhans cell
rules.note: Langerhans cells spread long processes between the cells of the epidermis.

rules.label: dendritic cell
rules.note: Dendritic cells are named for their long, branching processes.

rules.label: myoepithelial cell
rules.note: Contractile, star-shaped cells around gland units.

rules.label: ureter adventitial cell
rules.note: Cell Ontology files it under endothelial cell, but it is a fibroblast-like cell of the ureter's outer coat.

rules.label: basal cell
rules.note: Basal cells of layered epithelia are low, cube-like cells.

rules.label: basal epithelial cell of tracheobronchial tree
rules.note: Basal cells of the airway lining.

rules.label: keratinocyte stem cell
rules.note: These cells sit in the basal layer of the epidermis.

rules.label: endothelial cell
rules.note: Endothelium is a single layer of flat cells.

rules.label: kidney loop of Henle thin descending limb epithelial cell
rules.note: The thin limbs of the loop of Henle are lined by flat cells.

rules.label: kidney loop of Henle thin ascending limb epithelial cell
rules.note: The thin limbs of the loop of Henle are lined by flat cells.

rules.label: parietal epithelial cell
rules.note: Bowman's capsule is lined by flat cells.

rules.label: pulmonary alveolar epithelial cell
rules.note: Flat type 1 cells cover most of the alveolar surface.

rules.label: keratinocyte
rules.note: The epidermis is a stratified squamous (flat-celled) epithelium.

rules.label: lens epithelial cell
rules.note: Cell Ontology: 'A cell of the cuboidal epithelium that covers the lens'.

rules.label: club cell
rules.note: Bronchiolar epithelium is low columnar to cuboidal.

rules.label: hepatocyte
rules.note: Hepatocytes are many-sided; a cube is the nearest of the three epithelial shapes.

rules.label: ependymal cell
rules.note: Ependymal cells line the brain's ventricles as a cuboidal-to-columnar layer.

rules.label: macula densa epithelial cell
rules.note: Tall, closely packed cells.

rules.label: kidney tubule cell
rules.note: Kidney tubules are lined by cuboidal epithelium.

rules.label: kidney collecting duct cell
rules.note: Collecting ducts are lined by cuboidal epithelium (taller in the inner medulla).

rules.label: kidney loop of Henle epithelial cell
rules.note: The thick limbs of the loop of Henle are lined by cuboidal cells.

rules.label: striated cell of salivary gland
rules.note: Striated ducts are lined by columnar cells.

rules.label: duct epithelial cell
rules.note: Small ducts are lined by cuboidal cells.

rules.label: urothelial cell
rules.note: Transitional epithelium; a cube is the nearest of the three epithelial shapes.

rules.label: transitional epithelial cell
rules.note: Transitional epithelium; a cube is the nearest of the three epithelial shapes.

rules.label: epithelial cell of alimentary canal
rules.note: The stomach and intestine are lined by columnar cells.

rules.label: epithelial cell of tracheobronchial tree
rules.note: The airways are lined by a pseudostratified columnar epithelium.

rules.label: respiratory tract epithelial cell
rules.note: The airways are lined by columnar cells.

rules.label: epithelial cell of prostate
rules.note: The prostate glands are lined by columnar cells.

rules.label: acinar cell
rules.note: Acinar cells are pyramid-shaped; a column is the nearest of the three epithelial shapes.

cilia.label: multiciliated columnar cell of tracheobronchial tree

noNucleus.label: anucleate cell
noNucleus.why: Cell Ontology classes it as an anucleate cell.

noNucleus.label: lens fiber cell
noNucleus.why: Lens fibers lose their nuclei and organelles as they mature into the bulk of the lens (Cell Ontology, secondary lens fiber: 'cell organelles are normally degraded or in the process of being degraded').

noNucleus.label: onychocyte
noNucleus.why: Nail plate cells are fully keratinized, flattened dead cells without a nucleus, like the corneocytes of the skin.
